main_text.p: juria affecti, ad condonandum proximo essemus adeo difficiles, ac si omnis apud nos charitas exularet? Suadet hoc Genef. etiam exemplum Josephi, 45. v.12. Moisis, Davidis, aliorumque 1. Sam. virorum piorum qui cum potuissent, contumelias tamen sibi illatas, severè non vindicarunt. Idem suadent exempla Gentilium: Socrates enim rogatus, cur se percutientem in jus non vocaret, ridiculum, inquit, si asinum calcibus percutientem in jus traherem. Et Philippus Macedo, amicis suadentibus, ut maledicum domo exigeret: non faciam, inquit, ne circumiens, inter plures maledicar. Caesar etiam hoc potissimum nomine à Cicerone commendatus est, quod nullarum rerum, quam injuriarum, facilius oblivisceretur. Nec incognita Thrasybuli historia, qui cum deletis 30. Ty-

page.notes: Marginal references in the right margin, placed beside their lines: "Genef." beside "Suadet hoc"; "45. v.12." beside "Josephi"; "1. Sam." beside "Moisis"; and "24. 2.Samuel.16." beside "aliorumque", where the printed "2.Sa-" and "muel.16." are split over the line end. The split of "24." and "2.Sa-muel.16." between the two lines is my reading and may be slightly off. The printed "juriâ" has an accent I have written as "juria". The initial "J" of "Josephi" is printed as "J" and kept. The catchword "ran-" is taken as printed. No printing errors were detected.
